description: At the center of the card stands 【Crow Hes】 from the Yizhu world — the Fool. Hes, at sixteen years old, steps onto a path full of unknowns and confusion, standing at the edge of a jutting cliff and gazing outward. The successive deaths of his parents and the persecution of the Church and Royal House have not broken or discouraged him; instead, he moves without hesitation to embrace this unknown world. His upturned gaze and carefree expression directly embody his core spirit of 'innocence,' 'trust,' and 'living in the present.' His seemingly reckless stance at the cliff's edge reflects the dual nature of 'ignoring danger' and 'daring to take risks.' The flower that spirals along his arm and blooms in his hand symbolizes the 'purity' of his actions and the 'innocence' of his heart. The thorn-staff he carries on his shoulder represents the 'infinite potential' and past experience he bears, yet he does not carry it as a burden — showing his 'lightness of spirit.' The crow hovering at the staff's end represents both 'outside warnings' and dangers he has not noticed, as well as the instinct that 'loyally' follows him into the journey. Finally, the cliff beneath his feet, the thorns, and the distant snowy peaks together form the symbol of 'unknown journey' and 'noble ideals,' foretelling a road that is dangerous yet visionary. The light that swirls and resonates above his head like silk threads corresponds to his 'positive beginning' and the 'blessing of the cosmos,' suggesting this journey is guided by light. All these elements together build the Fool's complete card meaning: 'fearless beginning,' 'leap of faith,' and 'infinite potential.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Opener】 Arod from the Yizhu world — the Magician. To protect his companions from capture by their pursuers, Arod resolves to sacrifice himself and unleash all his miracles. Infinite energy converges in his palms, and he is determined to bring everything to a conclusion. His confident bearing and unwavering gaze directly embody 'focused will' and 'the ability to communicate between heaven and earth.' His gesture — right hand pointing skyward, left hand pointing to earth — concretely reflects the philosophical principle 'as above, so below,' symbolizing his power to transform spiritual ideals into material reality. The four elemental tools at his feet — sword, cup, staff, coin — are all displayed before him, directly corresponding to 'total preparedness' and 'the completeness of cosmic resources,' showing he possesses every element needed to manifest his ideas. In the world's lore, this corresponds to the 4 sacred scars he bears — he has awakened his miracles and possesses what is needed to overcome his enemies. The infinity symbol above his head corresponds to his 'limitless potential' and 'boundless creativity.' The thorn-plants spiraling and blooming at his side together form the symbol of 'manifested results' and 'abundant life force.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Holy Trinity Below the Throne · Silent Sea】 from the Yizhu world — the High Priestess. Her calm bearing and profound gaze directly correspond to 'introspection,' 'composure,' and 'wisdom that transcends the mundane.' The thread instrument she manipulates in her hands, half-hidden and half-revealed, symbolizes 'mysteries not yet fully disclosed' and 'knowledge that must be grasped through intuition.' The moon crown atop her head connects her to the subconscious, intuition, and feminine mystical power. The two pillars — one black, one white — beside her mark the duality of opposition and balance, symbolizing the gateway between the secular and the sacred. The dark rectangular veil behind her symbolizes the fertile potential and life force hidden beneath the surface. Finally, the densely woven complex patterns beneath her together form the symbol of 'calm reason' and 'purity of spirit.' All these elements build the High Priestess's complete card meaning: 'unfathomable intuition,' 'passively receiving wisdom,' and 'guardian of hidden truth.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Thorn-Circle Empress】 from the Yizhu world — the Empress. The Empress herself stands in a deep grey, unsettling environment. Perceiving a bleak and oppressive reality, she resolves to use her own hands to bring benefit to the people of this land, corresponding to the tarot meanings of 'comfort,' 'ease,' and 'the pursuit of sensory pleasure.' Her twelve-thorn crown 【The Thorn Sacred Yoke】 symbolizes the cosmos's governing force and the 'cycles of nature,' manifesting her 'supreme nurturing power.' The sword she holds is not for killing but represents her 'creative sovereignty' and 'dominion over life.' The raging war-fire behind her and her unyielding stance — her resolve to end the endless war and bring peace to the nation — together form the symbol of 'harvest,' 'abundance,' and 'boundless life force.' The ten symbols carved on the stone stele represent her ten sacred scars — both her innate gift and proof of her existence. The iron-thorn flowers shining before her connect to 'love,' 'joy,' and 'emotional abundance.' The radiant star-collar she wears at her neck symbolizes 'fertility,' 'potential,' and 'the secret of life.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Void Throne】 from the Yizhu world — the Emperor card. It is the embodiment of power and order. The solid cubic stone throne symbolizes a firm power structure and worldly foundation. The ankh-scepter placed on the throne represents the union of life and dominion, manifesting control. The traces of time worn into the throne's surface echo its pragmatic ambition and indomitable character. The barren mountain ranges surrounding the throne allude to the order and boundaries achieved under strict rules. No one has the capacity to sit upon the Void Throne; multiple forces compete desperately for the crown, symbolizing the invisible struggle for power. These elements together interpret the Emperor's core meaning as secular authority, institution-builder, and strategic overlord — constructing an unshakeable system of rule through reason, rules, and self-discipline.

At the center of the card stands 【The Holy Trinity Below the Throne · Living Sand Lake】 from the Yizhu world — the Hierophant card. The Hierophant is dressed in a cloak, concealing his form in shadow, pondering how to achieve his goals through hidden means. The Hierophant card is a symbol of spiritual transmission and collective faith. His triple crown corresponds to divine authority and the integration of body, mind, and spirit. The triple staff at his side represents the guiding force that bridges the three realms of heaven, earth, and humanity. The blessing gesture he makes directly echoes his core functions of 'spiritual transmission' and 'ritual inheritance.' The spiral chair behind him symbolizes the channel of wisdom between the visible and invisible worlds. The grey stone pillars in the background reinforce the stability of traditional institutions. These elements together reveal the Hierophant's nature as spiritual teacher, bridge of knowledge, and guardian of ritual, emphasizing the path of soul growth attained through established systems.

At the center of the card stand 【Black Thorn and White Sparrow】 from the Yizhu world — the Lovers card. The spiritual symbol floating in the clouds above signifies 'union, transcendence, and unity,' symbolizing divine guidance that transcends the individual and spiritual oneness, echoing the card's themes of 'harmony at a higher level' and 'soul contract.' Black Thorn and White Sparrow hold hands openly and face forward, their posture representing pure nature, the true self, and the dialogue between consciousness and the subconscious, corresponding to 'essential compatibility' and 'the existence of opposing dualities.' The fruit and tree of life beneath them point to 'the temptation of worldly desire' and 'the flame of spiritual awakening' respectively, together forming the eternal proposition of 'free will' and 'moral choice.' The distant landscape of mountains and rivers alludes to the domain of the soul's sanctuary and inner decisions. These elements together reveal the Lovers card's deeper meaning of 'soul-resonant choices,' 'alignment of values,' and 'integration of opposites,' emphasizing the clarity of life's direction achieved through sincere connection.

At the center of the card stands 【Night Fire】 from the Yizhu world — the Chariot card. Night Fire is the embodiment of the predatory will cast away by 【Grey】, the deity of this world. Its actions require enormous energy sacrifice and offerings, so it exists as a solidified stone slab most of the time. The Chariot card is a symbol of will-driven mastery and triumphant advance. 【Night Fire】's body possesses extremely powerful and muscular lower limbs, representing governing action through consciousness. The beams of light radiating from the torch at its center symbolize the harmonious harnessing of opposing energies, embodying the inner steadiness that governs contradiction. The four star-moon symbols in the background correspond to the balanced mastery of the four elements. The wing-shaped pauldrons on its shoulders echo the protection of intuition and the subconscious. The torch it holds is the mark of spiritual goals guiding material action. The boundary between the interior of the stone slab and the outer reality forms the threshold between the safe zone and the unknown domain. The grey star-canopy manifests transcendent spiritual guidance. These elements together reveal the Chariot card's core of 'harmonizing contradiction through will' and 'breaking through adversity' — through firm self-mastery, transforming opposing forces into the momentum of advance, seizing victory under spiritual guidance.

At the center of the card stands 【The Holy Trinity Below the Throne · Chaji Mountain】 from the Yizhu world — the Strength card. Wishing to understand the strange circumstances of her own birth, Chaji Mountain constantly searched the Church's vast library for answers. To access the most secret knowledge, she climbed relentlessly upward, and finally, upon becoming a Red Triangle, was able to glimpse the erased past. Her resistance against the Church was not fierce and outward, but restrained and resilient — she did everything in her power to fulfill her own goals. The woman who gently closes the lion's mouth, her expression calm and relaxed, together with the counterbalancing scales above the card, embodies 'the wisdom of overcoming strength with gentleness.' This lion is a special 【Aether Grey】 within her Church possessing tremendous power, capable of active thought and response, having accompanied 【Chaji Mountain】 for years, silently guarding her. Her grey-white robes symbolize the purity of the spirit and spiritual strength. The infinity symbol above her head corresponds to 'the infinity of inner potential' and 'the cycle of cosmic energy.' The lion's docile posture represents tamed primal desire, embodying 'the harmony of instinct and reason.' The woman's gentle caress alludes to 'guiding impulses with empathy' rather than suppression. The gleaming star-ring circling the lion's body and the deep sun radiating light echo 'the sublimation of vitality and passion.' The woman's pacifying posture without force manifests 'gentle, steadfast courage.' The rolling mountains and the runic stone sculptures below suggest 'the integration of natural nature.' These elements together interpret the Strength card's truth of 'conquering with the heart' — true strength springs from inner resilience, respect for the life instinct, and the deep mastery achieved through compassionate wisdom.

At the center of the card stands 【The Immortal Wood】 from the Yizhu world — the Hermit card. Yiven Pless joined the Four-Directions Society in the year 966 of the Circular Calendar, the same year he invented the portable illumination device 【Aether · Firefly Wood】, earning the title 'Immortal Wood.' In 981 he presided over the construction of 【Aether · Negation Circle】, which could briefly predict the future. His 999 prophecy of 'a newborn who will overturn the world' directly led to an unprecedented severity of inspections targeting the Impure that year. In 1018 he assisted Silent Sea in determining the method to erase Helvia, and ultimately passed away in 1034 — throughout his years in office, he tirelessly sought the hidden wisdom of the world, even offering his own life. The Hermit card is a symbol of introspection and the search for truth. The Immortal Wood, standing atop a snowy mountain, holds Aether · Firefly Wood, whose shining light symbolizes 'the wisdom that illuminates the path ahead,' corresponding to his role as a guide. The robes covering his head and face suggest 'removing oneself from worldly interference' and 'exploring inward.' The wooden staff in his right hand represents accumulated experience and 'supporting the spiritual pursuit.' The steep snowy mountain beneath him and the surrounding star-rings echo 'solitary spiritual practice' and 'a perspective that transcends the mundane.' The lantern half-covered by his front robe alludes to the deeper meaning that 'truth must be actively sought.' The folds of his plain robe reflect 'the breadth of experience sedimented through years.' The sky in the background reinforces 'the clarity of mind found in solitude.' These elements together reveal the Hermit card's core of 'seeking the way alone' and 'guidance toward truth' — through self-reflection removed from noise, attaining transcendent wisdom in solitude, ultimately becoming the spiritual beacon that illuminates others.

At the center of the card stands 【Aether · Negation Circle】 from the Yizhu world — the Wheel of Fortune. Yiven Pless presided over the construction of 【Aether · Negation Circle】 in the year 981 of the Circular Calendar — a device that could briefly portend the future. The device subsequently made several precise predictions of major events, including a female new monarch in 984, the attack on the capital by the Thirteen Halls of the Impure in 991 (this battle severely damaged the Fifth Hall), and the death of Black Triangle Daedalus in 994. Its 999 prophecy of 'a newborn who will overturn the world' directly led to an unprecedented severity of inspections targeting the Impure that year. With the severing of the miracle circuits in 1023, the Negation Circle became completely inoperative and was abandoned. The Wheel of Fortune card is a symbol of cosmic cycles and fate's turning points. The giant wheel at the center of the Negation Circle is covered with Hebrew letters and alchemical symbols, corresponding to 'the operation of cosmic law' and 'the cyclical period of life.' The divine dog on the left side of the wheel holding the moon symbolizes the protection of wisdom and the force of balance. The divine dog on the right side of the wheel corresponds to descending chaotic energy and the opportunity for transformation. The TARO letters rotating on the wheel's rim manifest the cyclical revelation of life's mysteries. These elements together reveal the Wheel of Fortune's core of 'irresistible turning points' and 'moments of soul advancement' — driven by cosmic law, each turning point is a necessary stage in soul growth, and only by flowing with the cycle can one attain higher illumination.

At the center of the card stands 【The Grass Cutter】 from the Yizhu world — the Justice card. The Justice card is a symbol of the law of cause and effect and rational judgment. 【The Grass Cutter】, a neutral deity, stands at center, holding a vertical sword that symbolizes 'the reason that cuts through confusion' and 'spiritual decisiveness.' Its double-edged nature corresponds to the double-sided impact of every choice. The grey scales in the lower right embody 'the absolutely impartial weighing' and 'the balance of consequences.' The crown atop its head echoes 'structured thinking' and 'moral authority.' The grey stone pillars stand as 'the barrier of truth amid binary opposition' and 'the guardian of rational boundaries.' The multiple circular rings of light in the background symbolize 'the fusion of human warmth and the execution of law.' The strange stone sculpture at the deity's base reinforces 'the solidity of secular law.' These elements together reveal the Justice card's nature of 'owning one's karma' and 'rational choice' — every decision leaves its mark on the cosmic scales, and only through objective scrutiny and moral courage can balance in life's lessons be achieved.

At the center of the card stands 【Salvation Grief】 from the Yizhu world — the Hanged One card. Before becoming a deity, Salvation Grief served as a Red Triangle within the Triangle Church and was executed for bearing a cursed child. After death, the soul it transformed into often appears on walls or rock faces in an inverted cross form. The Hanged One card is a symbol of sacrifice and shift of perspective. The T-form created by hanging inverted corresponds to 'wisdom in passivity' and 'the overturning of worldly values.' The halo above the head symbolizes 'spiritual awakening' and 'the arrival of insight.' The posture of hands placed behind the back alludes to 'releasing control' and 'accepting what flows naturally.' The expressionless face embodies 'calm in adversity' and 'wholehearted devotion.' The dark grey totem above represents 'suppressed action-passion.' The radiant crevices in the background hint at 'the flow of spiritual nourishment' and presage 'new life gestating in silence.' In its other form — appearing corporeal after falling into great despair — its body is covered in white feathers and bears a bird beak. The white glow at its crown symbolizes spiritual awakening; the spread of wings alludes to releasing control; the silk threads pulling at its body represent suppressed passion; the dazzling white feathers at its tail presage new life. These elements together reveal the Hanged One's mystery of 'advancing by retreating' — voluntary suspension is not an impasse but a necessary process of gaining higher wisdom through a shift in perspective, waiting in suspension for the soul's transformation and revelation.

At the center of the card stands 【The House】 from the Yizhu world — the Death card. The Death card is the ultimate symbol of transformation and rebirth. The master of 【The House】, cloaked in black robes and bearing multiple wings, holds the black longsword 【Black Cherry】 and presents it to those who are near death or in despair. Those who can withstand 【Black Cherry】's soul-shaking can transform and be reborn, symbolizing 'the continuation of life through death' and 'the indestructibility of the spirit.' The pure white wings echo 'the power of purification' and 'the sanctity of the vessel of new life.' The rotting black swords strewn across the ground are the final tombstones of those who could not endure, representing 'the end of worldly power' and 'resistance to change.' The tilted papal instrument standing rigidly to the right suggests 'the collapse of the old belief system.' The seamless nature of the wings manifests 'the absolute impartiality of death.' These elements together reveal the Death card's nature of 'forced sublimation' — all endings that appear like destruction are in reality the necessary reorganization of life's sequence; only by accepting the stripping away can one touch eternity.

At the center of the card stands 【The Twin Abysses】 from the Yizhu world — the Temperance card. The scene depicted is the 【Twin Abysses】 where the Impure are housed. Those Impure who accept the arrangements of the Royal House, comply with the Church's will, and can provide value are arranged to live in the Upper Abyss, while those deemed 'without value' can only dwell in the Lower Abyss. The golden cup representing the Upper Abyss and the silver cup representing the Lower Abyss float between the two abysses. The spread-winged posture demonstrates the role of 'bridge between the material and spiritual.' The liquid flowing between the two cups forms an infinite cycle, corresponding to 'energy harmonization' and 'emotional integration.' The Twin Abysses, though clearly stratified, also form a subtle balance. The bright star-radiance above symbolizes 'enlightening wisdom' and 'the guidance of the soul.' The winding path behind leads to 'mountains of spiritual elevation,' alluding to 'the path of gradual cultivation.' The bright scene in the distance heralds 'new life after transcendence.' These elements together interpret Temperance's truth of 'dynamic balance' — through conscious modulation and patient practice, transforming opposition into a higher-level unity, achieving divine harmony in the river of life.

At the center of the card stands 【The Dealer】 from the Yizhu world — the Devil card. As a neutral deity who always brings calamity, 【The Dealer】 is often crowned with the deep symbolism of material bondage and the shackles of desire. It frequently appears before those who have fallen into despair, using their desires to achieve its own ends. The three seated goat-headed giants at center, with the inverted pentagram crown above them, symbolize 'wisdom imprisoned' and 'the false faith of materialism.' The burning flames of the fourth spatial plane correspond to 'misleading temptation.' The stone prison below, alternately dense and sparse, alludes to 'spiritual fetters that appear solid yet can actually be shed.' The long serpent coiling through the sea of fire within the prison echoes 'suppressed passion' and 'indulgent sensory pleasure.' The straight dividing line represents 'rigid materialism.' The deep black background of the devil forms 'the obscuring of the soul's light.' The controlling gesture with palms facing down manifests 'manipulation of the subconscious.' These elements together reveal the Devil card's nature of 'self-made cage' — all bondage originates from identifying with material illusion; only by awakening inner will can one break free from desire's chains and reclaim spiritual freedom.

At the center of the card stands 【The Thorn-Breaking Tower】 from the Yizhu world — the Tower card. The original form of this towering structure was 【The Thorn Nest】, the landmark building of the Triangle Church, used to imprison and monitor those who violated its doctrines. After being abandoned following an accidental fire, it was repurposed by the Circular Royal House into the site of a ranking trial, becoming 【The Thorn-Breaking Tower】. The Tower card is a symbol of disruptive revelation and the collapse of old structures. The tower top struck by thunder corresponds to 'sudden intervention of fate' and 'the shattering of entrenched perceptions.' The two falling swallows represent 'the fall of materialism' and suggest 'the collapse of the old belief system.' The bursting sparks form 'the lightning of divine revelation.' The jagged mountain rocks at the tower's base manifest 'the fragile foundation of illusory security.' The falling flames reflect 'the burning away of spiritual shackles.' The pitch-black veins in the background reinforce 'purification amid chaos.' These elements together reveal the Tower card's nature of 'forced awakening' — all false structures on the verge of collapse will ultimately crumble in the light of truth, and this very destruction is the necessary ritual through which the soul attains liberation.

At the center of the card stands 【Aether · Cosmic Tear】 from the Yizhu world — the Star card. 'Aether · Cosmic Tear' is a special existence on par with the 'Negation Circle,' constructed under the supervision of Prans Matthias in the year 981 of the Circular Calendar. As the core knowledge repository of the Four-Directions Society, it stored all the wisdom accumulated by the Society. It was invaded and damaged by the Thirteen Halls in 998, repaired in 1000 with heavy reinforcements, and finally ceased functioning together with the 'Negation Circle' when the miracle circuits were severed in 1023, ending its mission as the shared knowledge treasure of the Society and humanity. The Star card is a profound symbol of hope, rebirth, and spiritual guidance. The Cosmic Tear core suspended in midair, without protective cover, corresponds to 'authenticity in vulnerability' and 'the composure of dropping one's defenses.' The bird-shaped knowledge fluid spiraling around it symbolizes 'the nourishing flow from the subconscious to the conscious.' It coexists symbiotically with the Cosmic Tear like a living creature, retrieving knowledge fluid to give to its users; the spiraling, flying form suggests 'the arrival of wisdom and healing.' The star-shaped Cosmic Tear core at the very top, leading seven smaller stars, forms a 'cosmic guidance system.' The phantom of a distant planet suggests 'the sublimation of spiritual freedom.' These elements together reveal the Star card's nature of 'spiritual revival.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Silver Moon Altar】 from the Yizhu world — the Moon card. The Silver Moon Altar, as the Triangle Church's core instrument, enshrines the primordial triangle representing the Church's ultimate secret. The Moon card is a profound symbol of subconscious fluctuations and unknown fears. The high-hanging silver moon radiates an eerie light, corresponding to 'illusions that are hard to distinguish as true or false' and 'the dual face of the subconscious.' The twisted moonlight alludes to 'distorted intuitive signals.' The crow above the path symbolizes 'the shared unease of domesticated and wild instincts.' The crow below the path echoes 'primitive fears surfacing from the depths of the subconscious.' The winding staircase stretching upward represents 'the necessary journey through confusion.' The boundary between the silver above and deep black below forms 'the border marker between reality and illusion.' The twisted moon sculptures lining the path conceal 'the potential danger of spiritual contamination.' These elements together reveal the Moon card's nature of 'the soul's dark night' — at the boundary between the conscious and unconscious, all suppressed fears and desires will manifest; only by confronting the shadow can one traverse this realm of confusion and reach the true dawn.

At the center of the card stands 【White Night Triumph Crow】 from the Yizhu world — the Sun card. At this moment, White Night Triumph Crow has been arrested and imprisoned by the Church within 【Aether · Light Suppressor】, its burning life force and radiance temporarily obscured. The Sun card is the ultimate symbol of pure joy and life's success. The three-legged golden crow standing at the center of the sun radiating light to every horizon corresponds to 'the illumination of cosmic consciousness' and 'the absolute manifestation of truth.' The straight and flowing rays of light emitted by the sun in the form of a divine bird symbolize respectively 'clear reason' and 'flowing emotion' in harmonious unity. The divine bird at the very center with pure white wings displays 'the authentic state that transcends worldly bonds' and 'the surging momentum of life.' The surrounding blazing radiance echoes 'the awakened crown chakra energy.' The divine birds at the periphery flying toward the center form 'the material world's pursuit of spiritual light.' The invisible barrier surrounding 【Aether · Light Suppressor】 alludes to 'the protected realm of purity.' These elements together reveal the Sun card's nature of 'absolute brightness' — when the soul resonates perfectly with cosmic will, all clouds dissipate and life radiates its original completeness and vitality in the light of truth.

At the center of the card stands 【Voiceless Prayer】 from the Yizhu world — the Judgement card. As a neutral deity, Voiceless Prayer appears before those who are drifting and struggling at the edge of death, playing for them a symphony of awakening and rebirth. The Judgement card is a profound symbol of soul awakening and ultimate redemption. The horn sounding vertically downward at the top of the image corresponds to 'the descent of divine revelation' and 'the settlement of karmic cause and effect.' The person below, with a withered body but spreading enormous wings, symbolizes 'liberation from the old self,' 'complete acceptance of truth,' and 'the soul's yearning for redemption.' The solemn entity floating above the river channel like an hourglass corresponds to 'the vessel that carries the soul through death.' The river water sweeping and spreading from behind represents 'the release and purification of frozen emotions.' The prostrate, kneeling posture and the measuring instrument to the right used to gauge the sins of judgment together form 'the equality of the soul before truth.' These elements together reveal the Judgement card's nature of 'the ripening of karma' — when the soul reaches the threshold of evolution, every past choice will receive ultimate assessment; only by confronting the core subject of life can one traverse the illusion of death and attain true rebirth in the awakening trumpet.

At the center of the card stands 【The Most Ancient Witch】 from the Yizhu world — the World card. The Most Ancient Witch has gathered all the circuits of the world, concentrating all miracles in herself, but at this moment she is in a sealed state, hiding her true body within stone slabs, awaiting the birth and awakening of the final moment. The World card is the ultimate symbol of complete achievement and soul integration. The stone slabs rotating in all directions around her conceal miracle energy representing infinite cycles, corresponding to 'the complete cycle of life' and 'the eternal flow of energy.' The star-like patterns radiating from her head symbolize 'the crown of victory' and 'the completeness of worldly achievement.' The flawless inner stone slab represents 'the solidity of the cosmic pillar.' The flowing text on the inner stone slab represents 'the highest achievement of the spirit.' The posture of those bowing toward 【The Most Ancient Witch】 at the center in the background alludes to 'the sacred order born from chaos.' The space between the inner and outer stone slabs suggests 'the eternal law that the endpoint is also a new beginning.' 【The Most Ancient Witch】's posture of subtle balance manifests 'the perfect harmony of inner and outer.' These elements together reveal the World card's nature of 'ultimate completion' — when individual consciousness fully resonates with cosmic law, the soul will experience absolute wholeness and freedom in the eternal dance.

At the center of the image stands 【Aether·True Self】, the Ace of Wands in the Yizhu world. In the enlistment test of Circular Calendar year 905, Ella — without any systematic training — displayed astonishing natural resistance to the side effects of 【Aether·True Self】, retaining a thread of reason even in a berserk state; she was regarded as a star of tremendous potential. Directly conscripted into the Bear Warrior Order, she is currently in a period of observation and cultivation. Her file notes: "Contains raw energy — awaiting guidance to be awakened." She represents new beginnings, immense potential, and the spark of action. Ella symbolizes the fresh blood flowing into the Möbius and the possibility of future development. This wand burning with roaring flames — 【Aether·True Self】 — holds the power to drive its bearer into a bursting state that unlocks the potential of life, symbolizing "the heaven-sent moment for action" and "the infusion of cosmic energy." The continuously rolling flames at the top of the wand correspond to "the eruption of life-force" and "the growth potential of plans," heralding that action will bring abundant results. The continuously burning flame patterns in the background represent "clear vision of a distant goal," while the ever-spiraling upward flame sphere on the right hints at "a peak of achievement worth climbing." These elements together interpret the Ace of Wands' essence of "sacred momentum": when the will of the cosmos is embodied through the wand, every new beginning will receive the support of nature's laws, growing in the soil of reality into an unstoppable torrent of creation.

At the center of the image stands 【Bridel-Hasaro Pursuit】, the Two of Wands in the Yizhu world. In the mission to capture defector Greck in Circular Calendar year 1003, Möbius military squad leader Leo once again demonstrated his outstanding strategic foresight. He planned three routes: the shortest but dangerous "Wind River" primary route, the reliable "Bedrock Path" backup route, and the concealed "Shadow Corridor" emergency route. Through keen observation of weather and environment, Leo decisively switched the team to the backup route before danger arose, successfully avoiding the devastating flash flood that struck that night. This decision not only ensured the squad's safety but also used the high ground advantage to lock in the target — his precise risk anticipation and multi-option preparation perfectly interpreted his reputation for "efficiency and precision." Leo standing on the battlements with a wand gripped firmly, gazing into the distance, symbolizes "planning based on existing achievements" and "proactive mastery of the future." The globe cradled in his right hand corresponds to "ambition that holds the world in its grasp" and "the establishment of a panoramic vision"; the second wand fixed in its base represents "potential courses of action" and "a stable foundation." The unbroken mountains in the background echo "the domain of challenges yet to be conquered"; the river winding at the mountain's foot forms "the natural flow of life's energy." The stone construction of the battlements displays "the fortress of achievements already built"; the contrast between the lord's flame-like hair and his smooth, flowing garments alludes to "the balance of passion and reason." The cross ornament hanging nearby hints at "the crossroads of binary decisions." These elements together interpret the Two of Wands' essence of "the strategist's frame of mind": when momentum and vision converge at the high ground, every decision will measure the world with reason, extending the boundaries of power in the tension between mastery and exploration.

At the center of the image stands 【Forge of the Sword】, the Three of Wands in the Yizhu world. In the lower left corner of the image is Zersel, leader of the "Silver Shark" Knights — her exceptional foresight lies in the sublime art of integrating human talent. Overriding opposition, she recruited two "Impure" powerhouses, Pasalos and Frampese, firmly believing that "true strength lies in making different blades swing in concert." In the famous Battle of Cracked Scale Canyon, she personally bore the most grueling frontal assault and, drawing on Pasalos' environmental early warning and Frampese's intelligence on enemy movements, launched an assault at once precise and ferocious that locked in victory for the allied forces. Zersel standing on the cliff with one hand on the wand and gazing at the sea symbolizes "the consolidation of incremental achievement" and "the practice of far-reaching vision." The two wands rooted in the cliff face before her correspond to "the established foundation for action" and "stable resource support"; the stone steps winding down toward the harbor below her feet represent "the developmental path under planning" and "orderly progress." Three circular luminous exits in the distance respectively hint at "diverse exploration of opportunity," "cross-domain collaboration," and "future returns on investment." The tranquil environment echoes "a controllable external setting"; the unbroken mountains form "attainable development objectives." Zersel's simple yet elegant attire manifests "the fusion of wisdom and action"; her left hand lightly resting on the wand also alludes to "the guardianship of what has already been achieved." These elements together interpret the Three of Wands' essence of "strategic expansion": when initial action forms a solid foundation, the visionary will coordinate the whole from the commanding height, allowing every strategic layout to gestate into a grander panorama of achievement at the confluence of time and space.

At the center of the image stands 【Home】, the Four of Wands in the Yizhu world. As logistics chief of the "Day Wave" Knights, Frillanka's exceptional quality lies in her elevation of "logistics" into the art of building a "home." The Wave-Crest Fortress she oversaw, in addition to being a fully equipped military stronghold, is also a miniature community full of humanistic care. From wind-sheltered, sun-facing barracks and carefully calculated chimneys to the "Homeward-Gazing Platform" built at every base — the details she insisted upon together created the distinctive sense of belonging known as "for our family." It is precisely this deep understanding and satisfaction of the troops' physical and psychological needs that elevates the Wave-Crest Fortress beyond cold stone walls into a solid pillar of cohesion — perfectly interpreting the genuine solidity and achievement built on the foundation of humanity symbolized by the Four of Wands. The four wands rising majestically, flames streaming from their tips — from this point Frillanka begins building her ideal home — symbolize "the stable framework of achievement" and "incremental fulfillment." The flying bird ornament at the lower foreground echoes "the celebration of victory" and "the harmony of community," corresponding to "the harvest of diligent cultivation" and "the vigor of life-force." The star-patterned fence wall connected behind represents "the safe spiritual homeland" and "the end-point of the homeward journey"; the space partitioned off by the fence forms "the path that connects reality and ideal." The continuously twinkling starlight above together strengthens "the worry-free state of fulfillment" and alludes to "the natural reward that success brings." These elements together interpret the Four of Wands' essence of "festival of abundance": when action transforms into real-world results through orderly structure, life will bloom on a solid foundation into the most brilliant feast of celebration.

At the center of the image stands 【Calamity Dragon】, the Five of Wands in the Yizhu world. In the Fourth Knights "Calamity Dragon," Kres is like the very embodiment of the Five of Wands — treating obsessive worship of strength and internal competition as the only path to tempering the strong. His training is nearly life-or-death combat, repeatedly injuring colleagues; in tactical meetings he openly provokes, treating harmony as an excuse for the weak. This endless internal attrition ultimately ignited a large-scale brawl with the Second Knights over war spoils, earning him severe punishment. Yet the punishment also became a turning point. In a bitter campaign to suppress border bandits, his reckless brute courage erupted outward — single-handedly tearing open the enemy formation to create opportunity for his comrades — marking the moment when his Five-of-Wands fighting spirit began to shift from chaotic internal conflict toward the conquest of external formidable foes. Kres in the open field holds his wand locked in fierce combat with the four wands below representing allied comrades in the flames, symbolizing "the inevitability of clashing ideals" and "the friction necessary for growth." The dynamic of people raising wands in crossing movements corresponds to "the white-hot confrontation of viewpoints"; stark black-and-white contrast between the figures and the background represents "differences in stance and context." The constantly surging flames beneath the figures' feet echo "the vortex of energy sparked by conflict" and reinforce "the chaotic essence of competition." Kres standing and swinging his wand among them manifests "the courage to actively challenge"; the wands below — as if swept by a gale — allude to "rallying in the face of adversity." The characteristic that all participants appear to be brawling yet have not actually hurt each other reveals the essence of "constructive competition." These elements together interpret the Five of Wands' true meaning of "the growing pains of growth": when diverse forces temper one another in collision, every swing of the wand is a knock against the old order, gestating in the noisy arena the prototype of a new order.

At the center of the image stands 【Triumph】, the Six of Wands in the Yizhu world. Elikar, deputy commander of the "Day Wave" Knights, is the perfect embodiment of the victory and glory symbolized by the Six of Wands. In the celebrated battle to quell the Duke of Duran's rebellion, she personally led cavalry through a key flanking maneuver with consummate command and personal valor, turning the tide in a single stroke and becoming the kingdom's acknowledged symbol of victory. Yet her most outstanding quality lies in transforming personal glory into the spiritual wealth of the collective — she insisted that ordinary soldiers ride at the very front of the triumphal procession, and bestowed the honors on the families of fallen comrades. Elikar truly interprets the deeper meaning of the Six of Wands: the most lasting victory is the shared glory that allows the entire collective to taste the flavor of triumph. Triumphant Elikar holding the wand that symbolizes victory and glory, returning home in honor after quelling the war, symbolizes "the coronation of victory" and "public recognition." Her proudly held warhorse represents "pure action-force"; the horse's rearing neigh posture echoes "the proclamation of victory." The soldiers surrounding and following her hold identical wands, forming "resonance of ideals" and "the following of supporters." The five wands laid horizontally behind the knight allude to "challenges already conquered"; the star-shaped necklace worn at her neck manifests "the resolve to fight for one's beliefs." The contrast between the warhorse's burning flame mane and her plain white long garment presents "the balance of passion and growth"; the gleaming laurel crown reinforces the apex state of honor. These elements together interpret the Six of Wands' essence of "the moment of glory": when individual will conquers obstacles through action, victory is not only the individual's coronation, but becomes sacred fire that ignites collective belief — heralding in the clamor of triumph the opening of an even higher journey.

At the center of the image stands 【Swallowing the Awn】, the Seven of Wands in the Yizhu world. In the battle of "Throat-Cut Strait" in Circular Calendar year 971, when the main fleet suffered severe damage, Golda of the "Grey Whale" Knights volunteered and led three escort vessels to undertake the last rearguard defense mission. Through extraordinary tactical resolve, in six hours of brutal combat, she used overloaded aether furnaces to create burning barriers to hold back the pursuers. Facing the desperate straits of ships destroyed, crew killed, and comrades falling one by one, she stood firm at the most dangerous prow throughout — her will "like a reef," unshakeable. In the end, at a cost approaching total annihilation, she successfully guarded the safe withdrawal of the main force. Golda kneeling on the ground, both hands tightly gripping the wand while gazing at the other six wands buried in the earth — representing six fallen comrades — symbolizes "proactive guardianship of what has been achieved" and "fighting for one's beliefs." The six wands at her feet are not only epitaphs for former comrades but also a reminder of the grueling battles she once faced, corresponding to "the gathering of challenges from multiple fronts" and "the materialization of competitive pressure." Her position at the mountain's peak corresponds to "strategic initiative" and "the wisdom of defense as attack." The mountain slope gleaming with starlight and moonlight represents "an environment where vitality and challenge coexist." The posture of the wand held vertically against the shoulder alludes to "establishing one's defense line with oneself at its center," while the right hand not quite fully gripping the wand reveals "the possibility of a counterattack concealed within defense." These elements together interpret the Seven of Wands' essence of "the philosophy of the steadfast guardian": when what has been achieved is coveted from multiple sides, true courage lies in fortifying the defense line with a resolute posture — completing the ultimate confirmation of one's own value in the process of resisting pressure.

At the center of the image stands 【Shuttle】, the Eight of Wands in the Yizhu world. In the Fifth Knights "Crimson Steed," herald Talos is, as his symbol the Eight of Wands suggests, the embodiment of swiftness, precision, and the free flow of information. In the spring joint exercise of Circular Calendar year 1004, facing seventeen urgent orders issued in succession within twelve hours, he and his mount "Shadow Shuttle" swept through treacherous terrain like a gale, simultaneously commanding knights accompanying him, dashing over eight hundred li — not only completing every delivery without a single error, but through keen observation feeding real-time information on each unit's movements back to command, making subsequent orders more precise. This dash perfectly interpreted the true essence of the Eight of Wands: the most powerful force originates from unimpeded swift flow, and Talos is the living lifeblood that keeps the entire command system operating flexibly. The eight wands represent Knights members rapidly advancing toward the set objective under the command of herald Talos, cleaving through the vast sky like arrows loosed from the bow, displaying perfect parallel trajectories, symbolizing "the complete release of action-force" and "high-speed progress after all obstacles are cleared." The uniform direction of their tips corresponds to "the intense focus on the target"; the state of soaring in air represents "free action unbound by constraints." The flames wrapping around the wands echo "the natural forward flow of life"; the architecture in the distance alludes to "a clearly visible endpoint." The transparent sky and the vast earth together form "the ideal environment for advance"; the grain and texture of the wands manifest "the purity of raw momentum"; the elaborately crafted tips in various forms suggest "the precious value contained in action." These elements together interpret the Eight of Wands' essence of "unstoppable momentum": when inner will aligns with the cosmic current, all resistance will transform into propulsive force, letting life's energy fly like a precise arrow toward its destined endpoint.

At the center of the image stands 【Watch】, the Nine of Wands in the Yizhu world. In the Second Knights "Night Roar," Auric — with twenty-five years of service — is the embodiment of the tenacity and defensive wisdom of the Nine of Wands. Bearing eleven scars, his most outstanding achievement was in the bitter winter of Circular Calendar year 991, when he infiltrated alone into the northern rebel-occupied territory. Through instinctive integration with the environment and extraordinary survival artistry, he lay in hiding in impossible conditions for two months, finally bringing back intelligence that decided the course of the battle. Today he has distilled a lifetime of experience into the teaching materials "The Watching Eye," with the core philosophy of "making vigilance part of the bloodstream." Auric standing in the night color, tightly gripping the wand and leaning against it — countless scars and ailments never having broken this old sentinel — symbolizes "vigilance after enduring trials" and "defense that never slackens." His left hand resting on the wand and the scars implicit on his body correspond to "the memory of past trauma"; the posture of remaining intensely alert manifests "heightened awareness refined through tempering." The eight wands below him, like a forest of fence posts, form "the protective barrier built by experience"; their uneven arrangement alludes to "the accumulation of battle across different phases." His position at the highest point represents "the high ground of the mind"; the posture of the wounded figure standing vertically reveals "direct connection with the energy of the world"; the energy flames rising upward all around represent "the fusion of passion and wisdom." These elements together interpret the Nine of Wands' essence as "the guardian's maxim": when combat experience settles into wisdom for survival, every scar transforms into a warning beacon, forging an inviolable boundary of life in the eternal watch.

At the center of the image stands 【Mountain】, the Ten of Wands in the Yizhu world. The commander of the Bear Warrior Order, as a representative of a subjugated clan, embodies through his circumstances the heavy burden symbolized by the Ten of Wands. He bears the multiple pressures of his clan's survival, royal expectations, and the management of the Knights Order — each decision like being torn between competing loyalties. In difficult moments such as the Battle of Black Rock Canyon, he must respond in real time to contradictory demands from all sides while fighting fiercely at the front. Yet evaluation reports show his will is extraordinarily tenacious, rooted in his unique path of balance — recording clan proverbs within military regulations, weaving royal oaths into ceremonies. He proves that true strength lies not in setting down the burden, but in standing straight despite knowing the weight is crushing — for the sake of everything he protects — becoming the most tenacious bridge between clan and kingdom. The bowing commander of the Bear Warrior Order in the image carries ten wands and advances with slow steps — since swearing fealty to the royal family he has continuously borne immense pressure from every direction — symbolizing "excessive assumption of responsibility" and "persisting despite being overwhelmed." The nine burning flame-patterned orbs within the wands represent the steadfastness and tenacity behind his bearing of pressure; his deeply bowed spine corresponds to "deformation under pressure"; the rigid posture of arms cradling the wands represents "the stubborn refusal to let go." The tangled arrangement of wands forms "energy entanglement that has lost its order"; the layout that completely blocks the line of sight alludes to "the loss of sense of direction." The undulating fields underfoot echo "real tasks waiting to be completed"; the distance ahead, slowly approached, represents "the safe haven that seems far away." The detail of the man's bare feet on the earth emphasizes "direct friction with reality." These elements together interpret the Ten of Wands' essence as "the burden-bearer's predicament": when the sense of responsibility is warped into the shackle of self-torment, every wand speaks a truth of life: true strength lies not in bearing more, but in wisely discerning what weight is truly worth carrying.

At the center of the image stands 【God-Deceiver】, the Page of Wands in the Yizhu world. As the young apprentice personally mentored by Commander Rodwood, Sil manifests the Page of Wands' signature spirit of exploration and potential for growth. He often proposes unconventional tactical concepts such as using 【Aether·GodDeceiver】 to create "cognitive contamination"; though most are not adopted due to excessive risk, core concepts such as "perceptual fault induction" have been incorporated into strategic reserves. Under the commander's systematic training, he has made significant progress in hallucination micro-operation, able to control error within a matter of seconds — though an incident that left teammates confused about direction warns that his control still needs refinement. This energetic young apprentice stands in the vast desert, both hands lightly gripping the wand in a posture symbolizing curiosity and exploration of new beginnings — eager to develop new methods of combat, he pours his energy in with passion. His billowing robe reflects the passion of the fire element; the short hair beneath the robe manifests a pragmatic nature; the streamlined ribbon belt at his side hints at inner wisdom and life-force. The flames bursting from the tip of the wand correspond to "the awakening of potential and a new opportunity for growth"; the distant circular wheel of flames represents "a goal not yet reached but clearly visible." The apprentice's slightly tilted head reveals acute awareness of the surrounding environment; his stable stance embodies a careful attitude toward action. The clear sky and undulating sand dunes in the background together form "a domain of exploration full of possibility." These elements together interpret the Page of Wands' essence of "action awakening": when the energy of the fire element manifests in its purest form, every thought contains the seed of realization, and every exploration is the sacred process of transforming potential into reality.

At the center of the image stands 【Sudden Rush】, the Knight of Wands in the Yizhu world. Knight Farmalor pushes the swiftness and striking power symbolized by the Knight of Wands to the extreme. In the famous "Molten Iron River Battle," he led his forces in an unbelievable dash, crossing what was considered an impassable swamp and launching a lethal strike from the enemy's weakest flank. Through the extraordinary reaction speed bestowed by 【Aether·FallingSun】, he can precisely process multiple streams of battle information during limit-speed charges, making the unit function like a perfectly coordinated organism operating at high speed. This blazing knight rides astride a galloping Swiftbird, the flames into which the wand transforms wrapping around him — symbolizing the complete release of action-force and clear directional aim toward the objective — vowing to launch an assault the enemy has no possible chance of responding to. His swirling battle-garb blazes with the pure energy of the fire element, fluttering like flame, displaying unstoppable passion and courage. The Swiftbird's posture of leaping airborne corresponds to "the swiftness of action and the resolve to break through convention"; the lingering flames under the wings bear witness to the powerful momentum of advance. His head-held-high, stop-at-nothing posture echoes soaring fighting spirit; the monochrome background presents clarity of consciousness and a bright future. These elements together interpret the Knight of Wands' essence of "the fire element's ultimate manifestation": when will and action are perfectly unified, every moment contains the power to shift the landscape, and every charge is a redefinition of life's boundary.

At the center of the image stands 【Homeland】, the Queen of Wands in the Yizhu world. Commander Melodar, through leadership rooted in deep emotional bonds, has forged the "Grey Whale" Knights into a unified whole full of loyalty and conviction. She knows not only the name of every crew member, but in the crisis of a storm night she led from the front, shouting "Live and die with the Grey Whale," earning the affectionate title "Our Commander." Tactically she displays acuity beyond her years — as in the Battle of Broken Ice Bay, where she precisely delegated command authority to unlock the initiative of the entire fleet for coordinated combat. She fuses ancient seafaring wisdom with modern technology; her leadership philosophy holds that true strength lies in "every ship willingly becoming an extension of the wand." This mature woman, her gaze resolute and directed upward, the sun-facing wand behind her symbolizing the full acceptance and guidance of life's passion — she conquered comrades-in-arms through sheer force of character, and through her vitality forged them into a solid whole. Her gleaming, exquisite crown and long robe interweave the vitality and dominion of the fire element; her hair curling like flame corresponds to vigorous life-force and abundant creativity. The streamlined tip of the wand echoes inner courage and strength; the wing-like form subtly formed by the wand hints at the possibility of spiritual sublimation. The Queen's stable posture manifests wisdom rooted in reality; the streamlined light-curtain behind her presents the dual qualities of passion and protection. Her focused gaze directed forward embodies a deep understanding of the meaning of action. These elements together interpret the Queen of Wands' essence of "warm strength": when the energy of the fire element manifests through mature form, every action becomes a source of nourishment for life, creating the most lasting achievement in the fusion of firmness and gentleness.

At the center of the image stands 【Brain in the Shadow】, the King of Wands in the Yizhu world. Commander Rodwood is the embodiment of the mature authority and strategic vision symbolized by the King of Wands; the core of his command philosophy is "cognitive domain warfare." The Battle of Red Rock Canyon he led has become a classic — through seventeen days of strategic deception luring the enemy deep in, he proved that "victory is determined before the horn sounds." In his hands 【Aether·GodDeceiver】 was elevated to a strategic weapon, capable of weaving multi-layered false intelligence and even using enemy spies to transmit misinformation in reverse — thus earning him the Empress's epithet "Brain in the Shadow." He is further dedicated to cultivating strategic talent, systematically teaching the art of deception. This mature ruler holding the wand at an angle symbolizes precise mastery and strategic guidance of action's power — his far-seeing wisdom and the god-deceiving wand he holds always contrive to create excellent opportunity for comrades in the most desperate situations. His flame-burning helmet forms the classic configuration of the fire element; the burning golden circular crown atop his head echoes wisdom that combines action-force and patience. The oddly shaped and razor-sharp wand and the circular flame wheel in the background focused on the wand together reinforce royal authority and primal strength. His upright, resolute posture manifests connection with the energy of the earth; the burning sky and the stable earth form a domain full of tension yet in balance. His gaze into the distance reveals the strategist's foresight; his right hand gripping the wand embodies absolute sovereignty over action. These elements together interpret the King of Wands' essence of "the fire element's ultimate sovereign": when action-force is refined over years into mature leadership, every decision will ignite the team's fire of passion, opening up the most expansive domain of life in the balance of the steady and the daring.

At the center of the card stands 【Aether · Holy Grail】 from the Yizhu world — Cups Ace. It is an instrument crafted by the Four-Directions Society for storing large amounts of information, but all were stolen in an accident. To this day, searching for the scattered grails remains an important mission for Society members. Cups Ace symbolizes a brand new beginning of emotion and spirit. The grail floating quietly in the clouds represents 'the bestowal of divine grace' and 'the opening of the subconscious.' The five streams of water flowing from the cup downward, gathering into a brook, correspond to 'the awakening of the five sensory experiences' and 'the abundant flowing of emotion.' The white dove flying into the cup carrying a star-radiance symbolizes 'the nourishment of the soul' and 'the revelation of peace.' The swallows circling the cup echo 'the pure state of the subconscious' and 'the sprouting of spiritual growth.' The undulating furrows carved on the cup body like flowing water allude to 'the channel between the material world and the spiritual world.' These elements together interpret Cups Ace's nature as 'the wellspring of love' — when divine power is poured through the grail, the spirit will break all restraints and nurture infinite possibility in the fertile soil of emotion.

At the center of the card stand 【Clarissa & Leona】 from the Yizhu world — the Two of Cups. Society linguist 【Clarissa】 and cryptographer 【Leona】 collaborated closely, jointly deciphering the inscriptions hidden on the bases of Grails No. 2 and 3, and submitted their report to the Society after reaching consensus. The Two of Cups symbolizes the emotional connection of equal harmony. The two people facing each other with cups, in equal posture and dividing labor to decipher the grail inscriptions, represent 'the resonance of souls' and 'the bidirectional flow of emotion.' The tilted grails in both their hands form an exchange arc, corresponding to 'the merging of intentions' and 'the balance of energy.' The water columns rising from the cups and meeting in mid-air symbolize 'the resonance of emotion' and 'the sparking of inspiration.' The gesture of each trying to touch the other alludes to 'the collaboration of consciousness and subconscious.' The star-shaped curtain below manifests 'the harmonization of opposing forces' and 'the magic of communication.' The cipher-stone above their heads echoes 'the taming of primal passion' and 'spiritual elevation.' The distant mountains form 'the solid foundation of the emotional relationship.' The contrasting black and white of their robes represent 'the dialectical unity of passion and purity.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Celebration】 from the Yizhu world — the Three of Cups. Society botanist 【Gaia】, chemist 【Beatrice】, and metallurgist 【Theodora】 submitted a new interdisciplinary research plan, preparing to crack and replicate the physical composition of the grail through modern materials science. Through protracted collaboration, the three finally crafted three almost identical grails, though with significantly reduced storage capacity and duration. While not a complete success, their collaboration accumulated valuable manufacturing experience for the Society. The Three of Cups symbolizes the fruits of celebration, communion, and abundance. The synchronized posture of the three Society ladies raising their grails represents 'community celebration' and 'the fusion of emotional energy.' The grails clinking in their hands form a stable triangle, corresponding to 'solid emotional connection' and 'the joy of multilateral cooperation.' The water-flow-shaped crowns 【Aether · Focused Mind】 spiraling above their heads can calm the spirit and concentrate attention, symbolizing 'material harvest' and 'spiritual joy.' The water flowing all around echoes 'nature's gifts' and 'proof of abundance.' The dance posture with upraised heads alludes to 'gratitude for life's gifts.'

At the center of the card stands 【Malvina's Rejection】 from the Yizhu world — the Four of Cups. Senior researcher 【Malvina】 of the Four-Directions Society rejected the Society's arranged 【Seeker】 project and instead launched an independent 'Relic' research plan, wanting to restore the Society's glory by searching for the vast knowledge network once stored in the grails, rather than simply searching for the grails as knowledge vessels. The Four of Cups symbolizes introspection, settling, and scrutiny of opportunities. Malvina hesitates under a tree, her closed posture unwilling to move forward, corresponding to 'the temporary closure of the emotional world' and 'the state of inner reflection.' The three grails lined up before her symbolize 'existing emotional choices.' The fourth grail floating out of the clouds represents 'a sudden new opportunity.' Malvina's hesitant avoidance of all the grails echoes 'deliberate distancing from the current situation and opportunities.' The hazy hills in the background form 'unexplored life possibilities.' The flourishing trees manifest 'the continuous growth of inner life.'

At the center of the card stands 【The False Grails】 from the Yizhu world — the Five of Cups. Society analyst 【Hortensia】 took over the five grail fragments found by the Society at great effort, and after a series of precise experiments, she firmly concluded that three of the fragments were forgeries. Hortensia's discovery caused a huge sensation; the Seeker project was ordered to halt, and people were immersed in the anguish of having spent enormous effort, time, and money to find false grails. Hortensia herself fell into a storm of public opinion, unable to hide her grief. The core meaning of the Five of Cups is 'focusing on loss' and 'ignoring still-existing support.' Hortensia in her black cloak stands with her back to the viewer, symbolizing 'immersion in grief' and 'closure to the outside.' The three overturned grails before her represent 'losses that have occurred.' The two grails still standing behind her, which she hasn't noticed, correspond to 'overlooked positive resources' and 'potential emotional support.' The winding river at her feet suggests 'the continuous flow of emotion' and 'healing brought by time.' The bridge over the river leading to distant buildings symbolizes 'the path to rebuilding connection' and 'hope for the future.'

At the center of the card stands 【Adelaide's Gift】 from the Yizhu world — the Six of Cups. In the year 835 of the Circular Calendar, retired researcher Adelaide donated to the Four-Directions Society her notes on folk legends, rituals, and customs related to 'grails,' collected over more than thirty years. She designated apprentice Rosalind to proofread only 5 pages per day to preserve the accuracy of the original records to the greatest extent. The core meaning of the Six of Cups is 'innocent giving,' 'nostalgic warmth,' and 'sheltered beauty.' In the courtyard, Adelaide bestows knowledge upon apprentice Rosalind, symbolizing 'the exchange of innocent emotion' and 'unconditional giving.' The clear stream flowing in the grail passed from the elder to the younger corresponds to 'the transmission of emotional nourishment' and 'the sharing of beautiful memories.' The other five grails arranged neatly also represent 'abundant emotional reserves.' The quiet environment forms 'a safe and protected space.' The banner fluttering to the right suggests 'the triumph of childlike innocence.' The winding path leading away reminds that growth inevitably means 'eventually stepping out of one's comfort zone.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Choice】 from the Yizhu world — the Seven of Cups. In the year 838 of the Circular Calendar, chief scholar Octavia of the Four-Directions Society, while presiding over the allocation of grail research funds, designed an anonymous weighted scoring process. However, she ultimately exercised her deciding authority, overturning the highest-scoring 'Material Analysis' project among seven and instead awarding the main funds to the fourth-ranked new proposal of 'Research into the Contents of Knowledge Vessels.' The core meaning of the Seven of Cups is 'the confusion of desire,' 'the emergence of illusions,' and 'the choice of the heart.' The seven grails emerging from cloud and mist each carry different symbolism — the shrouded glowing human form corresponds to 'projection of a spiritual idol,' the flickering building symbolizes 'unattainable ambition,' the standing staff represents 'the temptation of power,' the star-shaped gemstone alludes to 'material desire,' the gleaming laurel crown echoes 'worldly achievement,' the serpent suggests 'hidden fear,' and the quietly perched crow portends 'an unformed persona.' The enveloping grey mist symbolizes 'chaotic subconscious.' The spread-handed posture of the black silhouette embodies 'the passive receiving state' and 'lack of active discernment.'

At the center of the card stands 【Grey · Star】 from the Yizhu world — the Eight of Cups. In the year 841 of the Circular Calendar, researcher Josefa proposed the hypothesis that stellar cycles influenced grail 'revelations,' but gained no support as it deviated from the mainstream. She then used her personal resources to move into an abandoned observatory, conducting research alone through continuous astronomical observation and experiments with her own 【Grey Matter】 samples. After about 14 months, she shifted focus from grails to grey matter, discovering its energy fluctuations intensified under specific stellar configurations, speculating that grey matter states are modulated by cosmic cycles. During the 843 plague she refused to return and persisted, ultimately dying of illness but leaving over 800 days of complete observation records, which decades later became foundational literature in this interdisciplinary field. The core meaning of the Eight of Cups is 'purposeful departure,' 'the pursuit of deeper meaning,' and 'the courage to move beyond one's comfort zone.' The eight neatly arranged grails symbolize 'emotional achievements already attained.' Josefa turning her back on the grails represents 'lucid abandonment.' Her hand reaching forward and upward corresponds to 'the resolve to act.' The flowing darkness in the distance suggests 'a solitary journey of growth.' The bright road amid perpetual day and the stars of eternal night manifest 'intuitive guidance.' The river flowing underfoot echoes 'emotional attachments being transcended.' The spatial distance between the cup array and the departing figure constitutes 'the psychological break already made.'

At the center of the card stands 【The Diagram】 from the Yizhu world — the Nine of Cups. In the year 845 of the Circular Calendar, reclusive scholar Isadora submitted a revolutionary research report to the Four-Directions Society, pioneering a nine-dimensional classification system that standardized encoding of hundreds of core texts and built a multi-dimensional relational diagram system. Isadora refused the personal honors that followed, insisting the diagram's value lay in being a 'living tool' that required continuous updating. The Nine of Cups is called the card of 'wish fulfillment.' Isadora at the center with arms extended symbolizes 'the completeness of self-actualization' and 'the confirmation of inner abundance.' The nine grails arranged in an arc behind her correspond to 'the ultimate fulfillment of emotional wishes.' The magnificent garment adorned with star-chains manifests 'the celebration of worldly achievement.' The radiant star rising from the grail behind symbolizes 'the deep satisfaction of the subconscious.' The raised platform displaying the grails forms 'the stage sense of achievement being objectively witnessed.' The character's flowing hair echoes 'proud self-identity.' The shimmering background light represents 'the joy of the soul shining.'

At the center of the card stands 【Remnant Dust Resonance】 from the Yizhu world — the Ten of Cups. In the year 802 of the Circular Calendar, senior deacon Elvira of the Four-Directions Society presided over the final evaluation of the 'Remnant Dust Resonance' project. The project aimed to use modulated 'Aether Grey' to allow the deceased's family members a final complete family conversation within the three days while the soul was locked, to achieve emotional reconciliation. Elvira pointed out in her final report that the highest value of star-stone power lay in repairing humanity's most essential emotional connections, and proved that knowledge used to 'nourish' rather than 'plunder' creates spiritual legacies far more enduring than any weapon. The Ten of Cups is the ultimate symbol of emotional completeness and earthly paradise. The ten grails hanging beneath the brilliant rainbow at the horizon — Elvira through specially crafted Aether Grey enabling the deceased to reunite with the living — correspond to 'the arrival of divine blessing' and 'the realization of perfect emotion.' The embracing couple and the children gazing at each other form the core family unit, symbolizing 'the crystallization of love' and 'the inheritance of emotion.' The children's freely stretching dance posture echoes 'the flowing of innocent joy.' The radiant starlight in the distance forms 'an abundant natural support system.'

At the center of the card stands 【Manifold String Resonance】 from the Yizhu world — the Page of Cups. In the year 885 of the Circular Calendar, apprentice researcher Lina, out of personal curiosity during routine testing, used high-frequency sound to activate Grail No. 56 【Aether · Holy Grail】 and accidentally observed stable and regular anomalous energy fluctuations whose patterns resembled unknown encoding. She did not report through conventional channels but instead presented the complete record directly to senior researcher Sofia, known for her open-minded thinking, proposing in her report that it 'might become the basis for another kind of dialogue.' The Page of Cups is a symbol of sprouting emotion and intuitive awakening. Apprentice researcher Lina, standing before a wave-shaped stone platform, gazes at Grail No. 56 being activated by high-frequency sound, observing its anomalous energy fluctuations, symbolizing 'the awakening of emotional consciousness' and 'exploration of the subconscious domain.' The anomalous energy ripples leaping from the cup correspond to 'the bursting of inspiration.' The page's cautious standing posture alludes to 'cautious emotional probing.'
